text:
Jess: Quick Q — where's the best per-tenant view for KV/prefix cache hit-rate? Customer says their app token costs spiked, want to check hit-rate and traces for cache-miss path.

Omar: Dashboard -> Grafana > 'KV Prefix Cache' folder. Direct link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/9aBcPq/prefix-cache?orgId=1&panelId=5 Filter by tenant (top-right) or add ?var-tenant=acme in the URL. Panel 5 is the per-tenant heatmap.

Jess: Perfect, thx. Any quick queries for missed keys in logs?

Sophie: Use Loki: 
```
{app="kv-router"} |= "cache_miss" | json | tenant="acme" | count_over_time(5m)
```
That shows raw miss events.

Ravi: For traces, we have a span named `kv.lookup` with tag `cache.status` (HIT/MISS). Traces UI: https://traces.redwood.com/trace-search?service=kv-router&span=kv.lookup then filter tag cache.status=MISS and tenant=acme.

Jess: Awesome. Also saw an alert firing earlier — what are the current alert thresholds?

monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: KV Prefix Cache hit rate (tenant=acme) dropped to 54% (5m avg) — triggered at 60% threshold. Alert ID: ALRT-7231.

Omar: Current rule: `kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate < 0.6 for 5m` (critical). There's a warning at 0.75. We tuned this during the rollout in Q4. If it's noisy for single-tenant blips, we can make it `for 10m` or add `and avg_over_time(request_count[5m]) > 100` to avoid small-traffic false positives.

Sophie: +1 for adding a minimum request count. For multitenant bursts, false positives are common. Proposed rule: `avg_over_time(kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate{tenant=~".+"}[5m]) < 0.6 and sum_over_time(kv_requests_total{tenant="$tenant"}[5m]) > 200`.

Ravi: If we change the alert, we should also add a runbook link. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.com/kv-cache-miss. It covers which fallback model to enable and how to trigger a cache warmup job.

Jess: Can someone paste the dashboard panel ID for the hits vs misses graph? Want to embed in the support ticket.

Omar: Panel ID is 12 for the hits/misses timeseries. Use `&panelId=12` and `&from=now-2h&to=now` in the URL to capture the timeframe. Example: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/9aBcPq/prefix-cache?orgId=1&panelId=12&from=now-2h&to=now&var-tenant=acme

Sophie: If you need a single-tenant CSV export, open the panel -> share -> export CSV. I usually grab 30m around the incident.

Jess: Great — I'll attach both the CSV + trace sample to the support ticket. If this persists, I'll ping infra for a cache warmup. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Omar: FYI I'm going to drop a small Grafana annotation at the incident start time for tracking.

monitoring-bot: Note: Updated alert status -> acknowledged by Omar.

Jess: Closing loop — filed ticket #SUP-4412 with links to dashboard, CSV, trace sample, and runbook.

Sophie: Nice. If you want, I can draft a short note for the customer explaining caching behavior and suggested mitigations.

Jess: Please do, that would help.
